claims.text: A hybrid MLIP workflow trained on a carefully sampled ab initio database will substantially reduce the cost of free-energy evaluation across a fusion transition.
The hybrid workflow will retain accuracy comparable to explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD.
The training database will include configurations from both bulk and defect environments.
Direct ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluations will be replaced by an actively refined MLIP and enhanced-sampling scheme.
Targeted ab initio calculations near the phase-transition boundary will refine the MLIP in critical regions.
Enhanced sampling, such as metadynamics, will be used with the MLIP to calculate solid and liquid free energies.
The workflow will retain vibrational entropy, anharmonic effects, and electron–vibration coupling.
A representative set of ab initio configurations enables the MLIP to capture essential free-energy contributions, including anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling.
Active learning ensures adequate representation of configurations around the phase transition.
Accurate MLIP reproduction of solid- and liquid-state structural dynamics and energetics bridges their free-energy landscapes at lower computational cost.
The workflow will predict free-energy differences and phase-transition temperatures within approximately 5% of explicit AIMD results.
The workflow will reduce computational cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to AIMD.
The workflow will scale better than TOR-TILD for binary systems.
Explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD workflows are computationally expensive when vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration effects are included.
The proposed workflow is expected to be reliable for elemental and simple binary systems near their melting transitions.
Application to multicomponent high-entropy systems may require additional training data or methodological refinement.
MLIP fidelity may degrade for compositionally complex systems or systems with less well-behaved potential-energy surfaces.
Deviation greater than approximately 5% from explicit AIMD or established TOR-TILD free energies or transition temperatures will falsify the hypothesis.
